The decision comes after the State Department sent a notification to Congress about the planned funding, which is being sent to Kenya, Malawi, and Uganda, at the end of August. Days later, Democrats on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and House Foreign Affairs Committee placed holds on distributing the funds. The State Department says that the Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy provided briefings for relevant congressional staffers on the topic, and it ultimately requested the committees lift their holds by October 31. Now, the department says it will push past the holds and begin obligating the funds anyway. “The Trump administration is determined to follow through on its commitment to these bilateral health agreements,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement to Semafor, criticizing what he described as an attempt by Democrats to “block” the funds and arguing that it will go to “critical health efforts” like HIV treatment and malaria prevention.
